title: Distributed restore orchestration: on-prem + VPC roles
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook covers coordinated disaster recovery for hybrid private deployments (customer VPC + on-prem model-serving site). It focuses on orchestrating stateful restores across multiple domains: control-plane state (k8s manifests, config), storage snapshots (object-store and block device), KV caches (Redis/redis-like), and model shard rehydration.

What is unique here:
- Role-based choreography: different teams (network, infra, model-serving, security) own discrete steps and handoffs.
- Anti-entropy verification: lightweight checks to detect partial restores and divergence between on-prem and VPC replicas.
- Terraform invariant checks as preflight guards to avoid applying incompatible modules during restore windows.

Assumptions and prerequisites:
- Access: SRE lead and customer infra lead have bastion + jumpbox access for on-prem; cloud-admin has VPC admin; KMS keys available for decryption.
- Snapshots: latest consistent snapshot manifest (manifest.json) must be present in secure object-store with SHA256 checksums and signed by the on-call.
- Terraform: modules pinned to module_tag in module registry. Never run an unpinned module in restore window.
- Time window: schedule at low-traffic window + 4h validation buffer.

Roles and responsibilities (high level):
- Incident commander (IC): coordinate timeline, approve cutover and rollback.
- Network lead: route checks, BGP/prefix failover, VPN rekey if needed.
- Storage lead: snapshot validation, restore of block devices and CAS objects.
- Serving lead: model shards, KV warmup, container restarts, readiness probes.
- Terraform owner: run plan-only checks, validate module versions and state lock.
- Security lead: KMS unlock, validate integrity signatures, audit log enablement.

Runbook steps (ordered):
1) Triage + declare incident and IC. Document scope and earliest RTO target in incident chat.
2) Preflight (15–30m):
   - Fetch manifest.json from object-store and validate checksum: sha256sum -c manifest.json
   - Verify module pins: curl -s https://modules.internal/redwood/mods/curation | jq '.module_tag'
   - Lock Terraform state: terraform force-unlock -force <LOCK_ID> (with approval).
   - Confirm KMS key access: aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cek.enc --output text --query Plaintext | base64 --decode
3) Network isolation: place affected cluster into maintenance route (announce local route to prevent new traffic) and disable public ingress.
4) Storage restore (parallelizable, storage lead):
   - Restore block device snapshots to target volumes (cloud and on-prem) following steps in manifest: 
     * aws ec2 create-volume --snapshot-id snap-abc --availability-zone us-west-2a ...
   - Restore object-store exports into local CAS cache: rclone copy s3://customer-backups/manifest.tar.gz /var/backups/ && tar -xzf manifest.tar.gz -C /var/backups
   - Validate object checksums: run script check_manifest_integrity.sh /var/backups/manifest.json
5) Control-plane restore (k8s manifests, secrets):
   - Apply manifests in strict topological order: namespaces -> CRDs -> secrets (decrypted) -> configmaps -> deployments/statefulsets
   - Use kubectl apply --server-side=false --field-manager=restore-tool -f staged-manifests/
   - Wait for CRDs to be established before applying CRs (kubectl wait --for=condition=established crd/<name>)
6) State reconciliation (KV caches and databases):
   - Primary DB: restore from WAL+base backup. Start in read-only mode for verification.
   - KV/Cache: apply prefix replay only for warm keys, avoid full cold rebuild unless necessary. Recommended sequence: critical user prefixes -> model-metadata prefixes -> ephemeral session prefixes.
   - Example redis restore pattern: redis-cli -h localhost --pipe < critical-prefixes.rdb && redis-cli --cluster call CLUSTER MEET ... for cluster ring repair
7) Model shard rehydration and inventory checks:
   - Ensure model manifests match expected serving binary versions. If mismatch, do NOT rehydrate. Reference /var/backups/manifest.json -> model_shards[].
   - Start lightweight shard loader in dry mode to validate checksums: ./shard-loader --dry-run --manifest /var/backups/manifest.json
   - Rehydrate shards into local model cache; prioritize shards for high-priority routes first.
8) Smoke and integration tests (serving lead):
   - Health checks: /health, /ready for each pod.
   - Tokenized smoke tests: run 10 representative requests per route and verify logits/embeddings within expected thresholds (compare to golden hashes in manifest).
   - Load test: ramp to 10% production throughput for 20m to verify latency tail, batching behavior.
9) Cutover and monitoring (IC + network lead):
   - Open ingress (route re-add) for canary subset (1%) and monitor metrics for 30m.
   - If stable, incrementally increase traffic at operator discretion; keep rollback window for 2h.
10) Post-restore verification (full validation):
   - End-to-end audit: cross-check request ids, trace sampling (x-trace-id) across control plane and on-prem.
   - Data concordance: verify record counts for critical tables and model metadata hashes.

Rollback plan (if any step fails):
- Abort rehydration and return to network isolation.
- Re-lock state and attempt warm failback to last known-good snapshot (manifest.previous_manifest)
- If Terraform drift detected, run terraform state rm <resource> to remove damaged resource, then reapply pinned module version after approval.

Terraform module notes (practical guidance):
- Pin modules by digest or tag. Example: module "storage" { source = "git::https://...//tf-modules/storage?ref=v1.4.2" }
- Keep a small readonly bootstrap workspace used only for preflight checks that can run terraform plan against remote state without applying.
- In restore windows, never run terraform apply that upgrades provider versions or module major versions. Approvals for bumping providers must go through change-control.
- Use state locks diligently. If a lock is stale, verify owner and timestamp before force-unlock.
- Module snippet for restoring an EBS from snapshot (for reference, do not apply blindly):
resource "aws_volume_attachment" "restore" {
  device_name = "/dev/xvdf"
  instance_id = var.instance_id
  volume_id   = data.aws_ebs_snapshot.restore_snapshot.id
}

Upgrade plan intersection notes (when an upgrade is in-flight):
- If control-plane upgrade is scheduled and a restore is required mid-upgrade, prefer pausing the upgrade. Do not interleave stateful restore with rolling k8s-staged upgrades.
- When upgrading kernel/driver versions on on-prem hosts, perform a canary host first and validate NVME driver compatibility with model-serving runtime.
- Keep upgrade and restore runbooks separate but cross-referenced. If both must run, IC decides serial order; default: restore then upgrade.

Verification checklist (quick):
- [ ] manifest present and checksums verified
- [ ] Terraform plan shows only expected changes
- [ ] KMS keys unlocked and signatures validated
- [ ] Storage volumes attached and fs integrity OK (fsck output OK)
- [ ] k8s pods show "Ready" and readiness probes pass
- [ ] Model shard checksums match manifest
- [ ] Sample inference requests within golden thresholds
- [ ] Tracing and audit logs capture sampled requests

Known failure modes and mitigations:
- Partial object-store restore: detect using manifest parity; mitigate by streaming-only critical prefixes and scheduling full backfill asynchronously.
- Terraform drift causes resource mismatch: do not attempt state surgery without Terraform owner and IC approval; prefer rebuild path when faster.
- Model shard checksum mismatch: stop, mark shard corrupt, attempt secondary copy from registry or re-pull from upstream.

Appendix: useful commands and scripts
- Verify manifest checksums: cat /var/backups/manifest.json | jq -r '.files[] | .path + "  " + .sha256' | sha256sum -c -
- Preflight terraform plan (read-only): cd infra && terraform init -input=false && terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars -lock=true
- Redis warm replay tool: /usr/local/bin/redis-prefix-replay --manifest /var/backups/manifest.json --prefixes critical-prefixes.txt

References and ragged links:
- Confluence playbook: CONFLUENCE-PII-DR-PLAYBOOK-8421
- Terraform PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/112
- Incident checklist template: https://confluence.internal/incidents/checklist

Notes and open questions (working items):
- Need a canonical signed manifest format with expired signatures rejected automatically.
- Explore partial-cold-warm hybrid caching strategy to reduce rehydration time for large models.
- Automate preflight terraform checks in a CI job gated behind manual approval for restore windows.

Owner: Asha Patel (eng-private-deployments). Please update this doc after each DR rehearsal with timestamped notes and any changed commands.
